name: Azure Pipelines definitions
description: The Azure Pipelines YAML the repository carries, read as Azure writes it: what starts a run, the stages and jobs it declares, the pool each job lands on and how long it may run, and every task a step reaches for with the version it asks for, alongside the macro, template and runtime expressions a script interpolates. Names and shapes only, never a secret, an input value or a variable value.

pipelines.description: Comma separated globs matched against every file in the working directory and against bare file names, naming the pipeline definitions to read. Azure has no fixed location for them, so if your repository keeps them elsewhere, name them here. Anything matched that is not YAML is still left out.

facts.source: `report` when a pipeline definition was read, `none` when there was none.
facts.reason: Why nothing was read, present only when `source` is `none`.
facts.reports: Every definition that was read, in path order.
facts.reports[].path: Path of the definition, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.reports[].modified: When it was last written, ISO 8601.
facts.pipelines: The pipelines themselves, one entry per file that was read.
facts.pipelines[].path: Path of the file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.pipelines[].name: The `name` the pipeline gives its runs, exactly as written, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].triggers: Which of `trigger`, `pr`, `schedules` and `resources` the file declares. A file declaring none of them runs only when somebody starts it.
facts.pipelines[].variables: Names of the variables the pipeline declares, whether written as a mapping, as `name` entries, or as a `group` or `template` it pulls in. Names only, never values.
facts.pipelines[].stages: The stages the file declares, in the order it declares them. Empty for a pipeline written as jobs or steps alone.
facts.pipelines[].jobs: Every job in the file, whatever it is nested under: the jobs of each stage in order, then the top level `jobs`, and a pipeline written as bare `steps` as the one job it is.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].id: The `job` or `deployment` key, or the stage's name for a stage that declares neither, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].displayName: Display name the job gives itself, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].stage: The stage the job sits in, or `null` for a job declared outside one.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].pool: The `pool` the job asks for, exactly as written: a name, or a mapping naming a `vmImage` or an agent pool.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].hostedImage: The `vmImage` the job asks for, or `null` when it names none.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].selfHosted: `false` when the job names a `vmImage`, which is one of Microsoft's hosted agents, and `null` when it names a pool Azure does not say is hosted or names no pool at all.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].timeoutInMinutes: The declared `timeoutInMinutes`, exactly as written, or `null` when the job declares none and takes the organisation's own limit.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].environment: The environment a deployment job targets, exactly as written, or `null`. An environment is what carries an approval check.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].dependsOn: Jobs this one waits for, by name.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].condition: The raw `condition` guarding the job, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].template: The template this job comes from instead of declaring steps, exactly as written, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps: The steps the job declares, in order.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].displayName: Display name of the step, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].task: The task the step runs, exactly as written with its version, or `null` for a step that only runs a script.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].taskName: The part of `task` before the `@`, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].taskVersion: What follows the `@` in `task`, which for an Azure task is a major version rather than a revision anybody can pin further, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].template: The template the step pulls in instead of running something itself, exactly as written, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].script: The script body the step runs, whether written as `script`, `bash`, `pwsh` or `powershell`, truncated to 2000 characters, or `null`.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].shell: The shell keyword the body was written under, `bash`, `pwsh` or `powershell`, or `null` for a plain `script` step taking the agent's default.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].inputKeys: Names of the inputs the step passes to the task. Names only, never values.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].macros: Every `$( )` macro appearing in the script body, read from the whole body before it was truncated. A macro is substituted into the script before it runs, which is the script injection surface.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].templateExpre: Every `${{ }}` template expression appearing in the script body, which Azure resolves when the pipeline is compiled.
facts.pipelines[].jobs[].steps[].runtimeExpres: Every `$[ ]` runtime expression appearing in the script body, which Azure resolves when the run starts.
facts.stages: Every stage declared across the files that were read.
facts.unparsed: Files that matched but were not read, because their YAML uses something outside the subset the collector can represent. A file listed here is not an empty file: nothing was read from it, so draw no verdict about it.
facts.unparsed[].path: Path of the file that was not read.
facts.unparsed[].reason: The construct that could not be represented, and the line it is on.
